stem:
The diagram shows Neil's classroom floor plan: a large rectangle $12\,\mathrm{m}$ by $8\,\mathrm{m}$, split into Room A and Room B that share a straight side parallel to the $8\,\mathrm{m}$ sides. Room A has area $40\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$.

Which claim correctly finds the width of Room A along the $12\,\mathrm{m}$ side?

options.text: Width $=40\,\mathrm{m}$, taking the printed area as the width.
Width $=40\,\mathrm{m}$, and that holds even when the shared side length is unknown.
Width $=12\,\mathrm{m}$, because $12$ is printed on the long side of the plan.

teacher.key_rationale: Room A shares the $8\,\mathrm{m}$ height, so width $=40\div8=5\,\mathrm{m}$. Treating area as width swaps the quantity. Dropping the known shared side omits the needed length. Picking the printed $12$ captures a surface number.
teacher.figure_note: Added a 12-by-8 rectangle split into Room A (area 40) and Room B.
